---
title: "Explore autoregressive model order"
toc: false
page-layout: full
---

An autoregressive model of order $p$, written AR($p$), predicts the next value
$X_t$ of a series from its preceding $p$ values:

$$
\widehat{X}_t
= \beta_0 + \beta_1X_{t-1}
+ \cdots + \beta_pX_{t-p}.
$$

Here, $X_t$ is the hourly oil temperature (`OT`) in the ETT-small transformer
data. This explorer deliberately uses only `OT`: the six load measurements are
not inputs to these plain AR($p$) models.

::: {.callout-tip}
## What to watch

Increasing $p$ changes the length of the history window and the number of
learned coefficients. More history is not automatically better: the models
below are all fitted on an earlier portion of the same real series and compared
on later, held-out hours.
:::

```{=html}
<div id="ar-order-explorer" class="ar-order-explorer" aria-label="Autoregressive model-order comparison">
```

The ETT-small data contain hourly transformer oil temperature and six
load-related measurements. A later model can use all of those variables; this
page first isolates the fixed, univariate history rule that neural sequential
models generalize.

Source: [Electricity Transformer Temperature data](https://github.com/zhouhaoyi/ETDataset).
